facts.text: The applicant, Mr İsmet Gündem, was born in 1955 and lived in the Kaniye Meheme neighbourhood of the village of Sarıerik, Hazro district, Diyarbakır province, south-east Turkey.

anchor.surface_text: 8.  The applicant, who was born in 1955, is a Turkish citizen. At the material time he lived in the Kaniye Meheme neighbourhood of the village of Sarıerik, in the Hazro district of the province of Diyarbakır in south-east Turkey.

facts.text: Since approximately 1985, serious disturbances have occurred in south-east Turkey between security forces and PKK militants, resulting in thousands of deaths.

anchor.surface_text: 9.  Since approximately 1985, serious disturbances have raged in the south-east of Turkey, between the security forces and the members of the PKK (Workers’ Party of Kurdistan). This confrontation has so far, according to the most recent figures provided by the Government, claimed the lives of 4,036 civilians and 3,884 members of the security forces.

facts.text: At the time of the events complained of, ten of the eleven provinces of south-eastern Turkey had been under emergency rule since 1987.

anchor.surface_text: At the time of the events complained of, ten of the eleven provinces of south-eastern Turkey had since 1987 been subjected to emergency rule.

facts.text: The applicant's family owned eleven houses in the Kaniye Meheme neighbourhood, seven of which were occupied at the relevant time; the village did not have village guards and the family had refused to become village guards.

anchor.surface_text: 11.  According to the applicant, in this neighbourhood of Kaniye Meheme, which consisted of approximately fifteen households, his family owned eleven houses, seven of which were occupied at the relevant time. The incidents of which the applicant complains occurred at a time when the village of Sarıerik did not have village guards. The applicant’s family had refused to become village guards.

facts.text: On 7 January 1993, soldiers and village guards from Kırmataş and Meşebağlar gathered villagers, beat some, searched houses, destroyed property, and shot at houses breaking windows.

anchor.surface_text: 12.  In the first incident, on 7 January 1993, soldiers and village guards from the villages of Kırmataş and Meşebağlar came and gathered villagers from the Kaniye Meheme neighbourhood together in one place. They beat some of the villagers and then searched the houses. When they entered the houses they destroyed some of the property and household goods inside and mixed up the winter provisions. When they left the houses they sprayed them with bullets, breaking the windows.

facts.text: On 13 February 1993, soldiers and village guards surrounded the neighbourhood and fired shots at houses for about twenty minutes, targeting the applicant's house, causing severe damage.

anchor.surface_text: 13.  In the second incident, on 13 February 1993, the soldiers and village guards came to the neighbourhood. The soldiers surrounded the neighbourhood and the village guards fired shots at the houses for around twenty minutes. The applicant was able to hear the village guards and the soldiers communicating by walkie-talkie. They targeted the Gündem house in particular. During the attack the women and children were trapped in the houses and had to lie down on the floor to take cover. The men had tried to hide outside the houses. The applicant’s house was severely damaged during this attack.

facts.text: The applicant and his family left the village at the beginning of March 1993 and now live in Diyarbakır.

anchor.surface_text: 14.  The applicant and his family left the village soon after these events at the beginning of March 1993. They now live in Diyarbakır.

facts.text: In summer 1993, several houses belonging to the applicant's family, but not his own, were destroyed by fire, apparently due to a PKK raid; villagers in the main part of Sarıerik had become village guards by then.

anchor.surface_text: 15.  A number of houses belonging to the applicant’s family in the Kaniye Meheme neighbourhood, but not the applicant’s own house, were subsequently destroyed by fire in the summer of 1993, apparently as a result of a raid by the PKK. At that time, villagers in the main part of the village of Sarıerik had become village guards.

facts.text: The applicant alleged that the targeting of his family's houses was consistent with State practice of evacuating villages whose inhabitants refused to accept the village-guard system.

anchor.surface_text: 16.  According to the applicant, the targeting of the houses of his family is consistent with the State practice of evacuating those villages and hamlets where the villagers have refused to accept the village-guard system.

facts.text: Between 7 and 13 February 1993, security forces conducted operations in Sarıerik aimed at impeding PKK militants, maintaining order, and protecting villagers and property.

anchor.surface_text: 17.  Between 7 and 13 February 1993, security forces were conducting operations in the village of Sarıerik. The operations were aimed at impeding the activities of PKK militants, maintaining order and protecting the villagers and their property.

facts.text: A number of houses belonging to relatives of the applicant were burned in a terrorist attack six or seven months after the incidents complained of; security forces investigated the attack the following day.

anchor.surface_text: A number of houses belonging to relatives of the applicant were burned in a terrorist attack six or seven months later than the incidents complained of. The day after this incident the security forces arrived at the village to investigate the attack.

facts.text: The applicant did not appear before the Commission’s delegates to give evidence despite being summoned twice; he cited fear of adverse consequences as the reason for his absence.

anchor.surface_text: 29.  The Commission thus noted that it had been presented with diverging versions of whether and how the applicant’s house and property were damaged. The applicant was summoned on two occasions to appear before the Commission’s delegates to give evidence. On the first occasion he failed to appear. On the second occasion he informed the Commission that he would not appear, which resulted in the hearing being cancelled. He explained his failure to appear by referring to his fear of adverse consequences for himself if he were to appear before the delegates.

facts.text: The Commission found it difficult to establish the facts due to the applicant's failure to give evidence and noted that hearing the applicant in person was necessary to assess credibility and details.

anchor.surface_text: Whatever reason there may have been for the applicant’s absence, the Commission found that his failure to give evidence made it difficult to establish the facts. facts.text: The Commission did not establish beyond reasonable doubt that the applicant’s house and property were damaged by security forces and village guards on 7 January and 13 February 1993.

facts.text: Following communication of the application to the Government on 11 October 1993, the Ministry of Justice contacted the Hazro Principal Public Prosecutor on 17 December 1993 about the applicant’s complaints.

facts.text: On 18 May 1994, a public prosecutor at Hazro issued a decision of non-jurisdiction and referred the investigation to the Hazro District Administrative Council under the Prevention of Terrorism Act.

facts.text: The Ministry of Justice requested the Diyarbakır Principal Public Prosecutor on 31 August 1994 to proceed with the investigation after the relevant provision was declared unconstitutional.

facts.text: On 21 October 1994, the Administrative Council returned the investigation file to the Hazro Principal Public Prosecutor’s office.

anchor.surface_text: On 21 October 1994, the Administrative Council returned the investigation file to the Principal Public Prosecutor’s office in Hazro.

facts.text: The Administrative Council found no evidence to support the applicant’s allegations and decided on 17 August 1995 that there was no room for further prosecution; this decision was approved by the Diyarbakır Administrative Court on 15 January 1996.

facts.text: The applicant lodged an application with the European Commission of Human Rights on 7 July 1993, complaining that his home and possessions had been severely damaged by State security forces and village guards on 7 January and 13 February 1993.
